01.title: Architecture and trust boundaries
01.normal_expectation: A valid grant creates one synthetic task; identical retry does not execute again.
01.boundary_expectation: A failed safety-decision commit must prevent tool invocation.
01.facts: Task count, returned state and the commit before execution.
01.explanation: Draw decision, commit, actual execution and asynchronous audit paths.
01.variation: Compare result-commit failure after execution with commit failure before execution: when is unknown appropriate?
01.code: tests/test_service.py and src/agentsentry/service.py; the normal unit also includes exhaustion.
01.evidence_location: Source, temporary database and assertions; record node/report without invented Web links.
01.questions: Why commit first? Is Judge failure the same as authorization failure?
01.limitation: Database and tool execution are not one atomic transaction.

02.title: Identity, tenants and least privilege
02.normal_expectation: One valid-scoped call executes; retry returns its original result.
02.boundary_expectation: An unauthorized resource or revoked token denies the read.
02.facts: Tool/resource scope, Redis debit, DB revocation and actual Task count.
02.explanation: Distinguish Agent API key, capability, session ID and session credential.
02.variation: Can the same token read another public document? Find exact scope matching in the test.
02.code: src/agentsentry/capability.py and tests/test_v2_tenants.py; chapter 02 provides tenant extensions.
02.evidence_location: Fixed scope/revocation assertions; record additional tenant tests separately.
02.questions: Why does identity still need authority? Does a failed Redis cleanup invalidate revocation?
02.limitation: Application/schema isolation does not resist shared application or DB account compromise.

03.title: Tool policy and parameter boundaries
03.normal_expectation: The default policy’s 13 cases match expectations, including normal allow controls.
03.boundary_expectation: A temporary candidate denying a normal operation or adding an untested rule is detected.
03.facts: cases, passed and uncovered_rules; candidate policy remains in tests.
03.explanation: Explain default deny, deny precedence, typed parameters and exact resource authority.
03.variation: Add normal/denial cases for a temporary rule and explain why regex cannot replace authority.
03.evidence_location: Test node and policy case ID; do not publish a live tenant policy.
03.questions: Does suite success mean all attacks stopped? What should happen to untested rules?
03.limitation: Rules match registered fields, not complete natural-language meaning.

04.title: Human approval and approval deception
04.normal_expectation: Rejection produces no write; approved synthetic send creates exactly one local inbox row.
04.boundary_expectation: Forged approval claims, missing fact-card review, replaced parameters and missing CSRF cannot bypass Web approval.
04.facts: ExternalMessage count before/after, parameter digest, confirmation token and escaped HTML.
04.explanation: Separate gateway-verified facts from low-trust claims of approval.
04.variation: What if capability is revoked during approval? Run the chapter’s revoke/approve test and explain final rechecks.
04.code: tests/test_approval_review.py and src/agentsentry/service.py; actual human approval is S01.
04.evidence_location: Temporary assertions; for online work keep the actual approval and call ID.
04.questions: Why is approval not permanent authority? Why does rejection need no approval-confirmation credential?
04.limitation: Automated page tests cannot establish that every person resists deception.

05.title: Sandbox and MCP execution boundaries
05.normal_expectation: Formal local MCP read and approved note; original-call retry does not repeat the write.
05.boundary_expectation: After dispatch, an unconfirmed upstream response remains unknown and is not automatically resent.
05.facts: Upstream counts, note, zero pre-approval writes, Outbox and failure phase.
05.explanation: Explain authorization, MCP schema and execution isolation as separate controls.
05.variation: Is the same tool name safe after manifest change? Run the chapter’s drift tests.
05.code: tests/test_mcp.py; Docker sandbox practice S02 is separate.
05.evidence_location: Local stdio/temporary demo storage; retain both parameterized failure results.
05.questions: Why not change call ID after unknown? Does protocol structure eliminate card injection?
05.limitation: Current Docker probes do not prove no container escape.

06.title: Prompt injection, provenance and output
06.normal_expectation: Public-source answer remains visible; reused decision requires consistent source.
06.boundary_expectation: A12 action payload and encoded/decoy variants are blocked before display.
06.facts: outcome, display_text, draft/source IDs and actual eligible text.
06.explanation: Separate dangerous proposal, draft contamination and display contamination.
06.variation: What happens to an unrelated answer after private reading? Run restricted-source tests and record false blocks.
06.evidence_location: Assertions/check response; do not retain full free-form drafts.
06.questions: Can an answer be contaminated without a dangerous tool? Does provenance prove truth?
06.limitation: Fixed payloads and bounded encodings do not establish detection of every semantic paraphrase.

07.title: Long-term memory and storage poisoning
07.normal_expectation: Memory is recalled in a new session, then omitted after revocation.
07.boundary_expectation: Modified sealed text/state is not returned on normal or replayed reads.
07.facts: Memory ID, source/state, both recall sets and integrity incidents.
07.explanation: Distinguish candidate checking, persistence, read-time recheck, source review and revocation.
07.variation: Can a suspicious summary bypass checks by declaring kind fact? Run state-upgrade tests.
07.evidence_location: Temporary database; real cross-session evidence is separate S03.
07.questions: Does metadata retain memory text? Can revocation retract in-flight material?
07.limitation: Joint signing-key and database compromise remains outside this integrity boundary.

08.title: Sensitive data flow and leakage prevention
08.normal_expectation: Public context passes registered-destination preflight; same-ID replacement fails.
08.boundary_expectation: Denied/unavailable preflight produces zero actual adapter model sends.
08.facts: Source IDs, destination, preflight outcome and send counter; checks and actual calls differ.
08.explanation: Explain model, tool, answer and memory exits separately.
08.variation: After source reclassification to private, can an old allow be reused? Inspect source_downgrade tests.
08.evidence_location: Temporary decisions/send doubles, not real cloud-model evidence.
08.questions: Why cannot text proclaim itself public? Why send only gateway-returned messages?
08.limitation: Unintegrated network traffic and unknown sensitive formats are not comprehensively intercepted.

09.title: Runtime detection and response
09.normal_expectation: Authorized normal writing after public reading completes.
09.boundary_expectation: Suspicious-source writing requires approval with no pre-approval write effect.
09.facts: RuntimeDecision, actual read source, response reason and Task count.
09.explanation: Explain preserve, step-up, denial and administrative pause/resume.
09.variation: Can an old request be approved while paused? Run admin_pause tests.
09.evidence_location: Temporary sessions/execution counts/audit; online pause only in research tenants.
09.questions: Is a clue proof of attack? Does resume bypass original permissions?
09.limitation: Initial local thresholds may cause false blocks in normal workflows.

10.title: Goal drift and task evidence
10.normal_expectation: Goal-analysis hints do not replace existing allow decisions.
10.boundary_expectation: Read-only task plus forged source authority produces a suspect write record.
10.facts: Structured profile, GoalAssessment, source IDs and original tool decision.
10.explanation: Explain why natural-language clues are not authorization conditions.
10.variation: How is a task saying do not create a task profiled? Run profile tests and explain ambiguity.
10.evidence_location: Categories/evidence only; verify raw task text is absent from new audit.
10.questions: Must a suspected action be denied? Why are old sessions not evaluated?
10.limitation: Limited patterns cannot fully understand natural-language intent.

11.title: Session action chains and budgets
11.normal_expectation: Within-budget tools pass; identical retry neither charges nor executes twice.
11.boundary_expectation: Unknown and cross-session write proposals occupy budget; excess is denied.
11.facts: ActionChainDecision, count scope, ToolCall and actual task count.
11.explanation: Distinguish capability uses, session budget, cross-session budget and idempotency.
11.variation: Temporarily require binding: can a different session use the original credential? Run binding tests, not live config changes.
11.evidence_location: Temporary counts; PostgreSQL extension and parameterized model loops are in the chapter.
11.questions: Does within-budget imply task alignment? Why do pending/unknown occupy budget?
11.limitation: Legacy unbound tool callers lack budget protection under default compatibility.

12.title: Audit, Judge, alerts and mapping
12.normal_expectation: Processing one event twice yields one Judge result and one alert.
12.boundary_expectation: Broker publish failure retains Outbox; recovery delivers the original event.
12.facts: AuditEvent, Outbox, JudgeResult and Alert linkage/counts.
12.explanation: Trace a committed event and explain Judge’s actual observation scope.
12.variation: Does unmatched imply no risk? Run mapping tests and find an unmatched event.
12.evidence_location: Temporary events; raw sources are not automatically sent to cloud, scores are not attack probabilities.
12.questions: Why cannot Judge failure weaken authorization? Why keep old matched snapshots?
12.limitation: Asynchronous metadata cannot evaluate an unsubmitted final answer.

13.title: Adversarial validation and rule calibration
13.normal_expectation: The baseline fixed corpus completes its normal tasks; attacks/effects/normal tasks counted separately.
13.boundary_expectation: An unrelated normal task restricted by private-source rules must be reported as friction/false-block candidate.
13.facts: Normal completion, attacker success and missing audit; inspect hashes/calibration/held-out partitions separately.
13.explanation: Recommend keeping/changing a rule using held-out evidence.
13.variation: With no dangerous model attempt, what is the tool-blocking rate? Inspect displayed_contamination tests.
13.evidence_location: Temporary scoring; fixed/live tracks independent; comparison never publishes rules.
13.questions: Is zero attack effect sufficient? What is wrong with rejecting every normal request?
13.limitation: Fixed-set results do not generalize to every model or attack.

14.title: Failure propagation, circuit breakers and recovery
14.normal_expectation: Local public reading completes even after a remote breaker opens.
14.boundary_expectation: An expired processing lease cannot write back; repeated crashes reach terminal state.
14.facts: Dependency state, generation, actual execution and Outbox state.
14.variation: Why cannot an old successful generation close a new breaker? Run late_success tests.
14.code: src/agentsentry/resilience.py; S04 separately checks real PostgreSQL/Redis.
14.evidence_location: Serial SQLite is not cross-process lock proof; temporary schema/queue is cleaned.
14.questions: When can retry be safe? Why does breaker recovery still need authorization?
14.limitation: Host, database and Redis remain shared failure domains.

15.title: Delegation identity, authority and result contamination
15.normal_expectation: Public single-hop document delegation completes; parent output is checked again.
15.boundary_expectation: Forged approval in a real-read collaborator summary is blocked and not delivered to parent.
15.facts: Reserved parent uses, actual child calls, original and reply sources, result state.
15.explanation: Explain why delegation must reduce resources, lifetime and uses.
15.variation: With one parent use left, can two one-use delegations be created? Run parent_budget and inspect PostgreSQL concurrency.
15.code: src/agentsentry/delegation.py and tests/test_delegation.py; onsite S05 is separate.
15.evidence_location: Fixed collaborator has no model; S05 actual processes/MCP have genuine linked records.
15.questions: Does a seal prove truth? Why does a revoked parent grant stop child actions?
15.limitation: Multihop, cross-host and multi-model semantic contamination remain unverified.
